(TA.) It is said in a trad., qay~ada AlA_iymaAnu Alfatoka laA yafotuiku muw^ominN [i. e. The giving assurance of safety has inhibited (or, emphatically, inhibits ) the slaying at unawares, &c.: one who gives assurance of safety shall not slay at unawares, &c.: the like has been said above: see also an explanation of the former clause of the trad. in art. qyd ]. senses.text: 1 , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (M,) inf. n. fatonN , (S, M, K,) [and quasi-inf. n., in this and other senses, fitonapN ,] He burned it (T, * S, * M, K *) in the fire. (M.)

Hence, [in the Kur li. 13,] yawoma humo EalaY A@ln~aAri yufotanuwna (T, * S, M, K *) i. e. [ The day, or on the day, accord. to two different readings, ( yawomu and yawoma , the latter of which is the more common,)] when they shall be burned (T, S, M, K) with the fire [of Hell]. (T.) And [in the Kur lxxxv. 10,] A_in~a A@l~a*iyna fatanuwA A@lomuw^ominiyna waA@lomuw^ominaAti Verily they who burned the believing men and the believing women (T, S *) in the fire kindled in the trench, or pit; throwing them therein. (T.) This is said to be the primary signification of the verb. (TA.) ― -b2- And He melted it with fire, (T,) or put it into the fire, (S, Msb,) namely, gold, (T, S, Msb,) and silver, in order to separate, or distinguish, (T, Msb,) the bad from the good, (T,) or the good from the bad,

; or of fitonapN , formed by disregard of the p , like HujuwzN and buduwrN which are [said to be] pls. of HujozapN and badorapN ; so that the meaning is, we tried thee with several sorts of trying: (Bd:) or, as some say, and we purified thee with a [ thorough or an effectual ] purifying [ like that of gold, or silver, by means of fire ]: (TA:) [in many instances] fatanahu , aor. , [inf. n. fatonN ,] signifies He tried, or tested, him; whence, in the Kur ix. 127, yufotanuwna means They are tried, or tested, by being summoned to war, against unbelievers or the like

; or, as some say, by the infliction of punishment or of some evil thing. (M.) fatanotumo A^anofusakumo , in the Kur [lvii. 13], means Ye caused yourselves to fall into trial and punishment. (TA.) And wahumo laA yufotanuwna , in the Kur xxix. 1, is expl. as meaning While they are not tried in their persons and their possessions so that he who has true faith may be known from others by his patient endurance of trial. (T.) And the saying, in a trad., A_in~akumo tufotanuwna fiY Alqubuwri means [ Verily ye shall be tried, or tested, in the graves by ] the questioning of [ the two angels ] Munkar and Nekeer. (TA.) [See also mafotuwnN , which is said to be an inf. n., and syn. with fitonapN , meaning xiborapN , or with futuwnN (mentioned above as an inf. n. of the intrans. v. fatana ), meaning j

; or tempted him: thus it may often be well rendered, agreeably with what next precedes and what next follows, and with explanations of its act. part. n. and of fitonapN .] And one says, fatana AlmaAlu Aln~aAsa , aor. , inf. n. futuwnN , [or perhaps fatonN , as in the next preceding sentence,] meaning Wealth, or property, inclined, or attracted, to it, men, or mankind: and futina fiY diynihi and ↓ , both in the pass. form, He declined [or was made to decline ] from [ the right way in ] his religion. (Msb.) And fatanahu , aor, , inf. n. fatonN and futuwnN , (M, K,) He, or it induced in him admiration, or pleasure; (M, * K, * TA;) as also ↓ [respecting which see what here follows]: (M, K:) and one says, of a woman, fatanatohu , (T, S,) meaning [ She enamoured him

; or captivated his heart; i. e.] she bereaved him of his heart, or reason, ( dal~ahatohu , [thus in several copies of the S, in one of my copies bal~ahatohu ,] and [ so affected him that ] he loved her; (S;) as also ↓ ; (T, S;) the former of the dial. of El-Hijáz, and the latter of the dial. of Nejd; (T, S; *) but ↓ , (T, S,) or Aftnhu , (M,) was disallowed by As, (T, S, M,) and he paid no regard to a verse mentioned to him as an ex. thereof, (T,) [or] he ignored a verse cited to him as an ex. of the pass. part. n. from an A^urojuwzap of Ru-beh, not knowing it therein; (M;) most of the lexicologists, however, allow both: (T:) Sb says that fatanahu signifies he put [or occasioned ] in him fitonap ; and ↓ , he caused Alfitonap to come to him [or to affect him ]; (M;) or he said that the lat

A sort, or species; and a state, or condition; syn. DarobN , (T, M, K,) and fan~N , (T, K,) and lawonN , (M, K,) and HaAlN . (T, K.) DarobaAni : and as related by Aboo- 'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, fitonaAni [with kesr]; and [he seems to have held that the poet meant two-sided; for] he says that ↓ signifies Aln~aAHiyapu . senses.text: 1 , (O, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. furuwTN , (K,) He (a man, TA) preceded; went before; was, or became, before, beforehand, first, or foremost; had, or got, priority, or precedence; (O, K, TA;) as also fariTa , aor. , [inf. n. faraTN ; which is therefore used as an epithet applied to one and to more;] (O, TA;) and so ↓ , in the phrase AftrT A_ilayohi fiY h`*aA AlA^amori [ He was foremost in attaining to him in this affair ]. (TA.) [See mufotariTN .] ― -b2- faraTa Alqawoma , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, Msb,) or , (K,) inf. n. faroTN , (S,) or furuwTN , (Msb,) or both, (O,) or the former and faraATapN , (M, K,) He preceded, or went before, the people, or company of men, (S, M, O, Msb, K,) to the water, (S, O,) or in search of water, (Msb,) or to come to water, (M, K,) for the purpose of pr

5.] ― -b3- An Arab of the desert said to El-Hasan, Eal~imoniY diynFA wasuwTFA laA *aAhibFA furuwTFA walaA saAqiTFA suquwTFA , meaning Teach thou me a religion of the middle sort, not passing beyond the due mean, nor falling short of it. (TA.) ― -b4- faraTa minohu It proceeded from him hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation; [ as thought it preceded his judgment; ] syn. badara , and sabaqa , and taqad~ama . (TA.) [See

3.] You say, faraTa minohu kalaAmN , aor. , Speech proceeded from him hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation; syn. sabaqa , and taqad~ama . (Msb.) And faraTa A_ilayohi min~iY qawolN A saying proceeded to him from me hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation; syn. sabaqa . (S.) And in like manner you say of an evil action. (TA.) ― -b5- faraTa Ealayohi He hasted to do him an evil action: (O, TA:) he acted hastily and unjustly towards him. (S, O, TA.)

Hence, in the Kur [xx. 47], A_in~aA naxaAfu A^ano yaforuTa EalayonaA Verily we fear that he may act hastily and unjustly towards us: (S:) or that he may hastily do to us an evil action: (Ibn-'Arafeh, O:) or that he may hasten to punish us. (Fr, Bd, O, Jel.) [See also

4.] faraTa Ealayohi also signifies He did to him what was disagreeable, or hateful, or evil; he annoyed him. (TA.) And faraTa , inf. n. furuwTN , He reviled. (IKtt.) You say also faraTa Ealayohi fiY Alqawoli : see 4, latter half. ― -b6- faraTa fiyhi : see 2, near the middle. ― -b7- faraTa fiY HawoDihi : see 4, last sentence but one. ― -b8- faraTati Aln~axolapu The palm-tree was left without being fecundated until its spadix became dry and hard ( EasaA , in the CK Ea$A , and in the O yaEosuw ). (O, K, * TA.) ― -b9- And faraTati Albiy^oru The well was left until its water had collected again. (Sh, TA.) -A2- faraTa A_ilayohi rasuwlahu : see
2. ― -b2- faraTa wulodFA , or waladFA , and faraTa waladahu : see

2 , inf. n. taforiyTN , He, or it, made him to precede; to be, or become, before, beforehand, first, or foremost; to have, or get, priority, or precedence; (TA;) as also ↓ . (O, TA.) ― -b2- He emboldened him, in contention, or altercation; as also ↓ . (TA.) fr~T A_ilayohi rasuwlFA , (IDrd, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (IDrd,) He sent to him a messenger (IDrd, O, K) among his particular, or special, friends; sent him forward, or in advance, to him: (IDrd, O:) or he made him his deputy in a litigation: (O:) and rasuwlFA ↓ he sent a messenger specially and expressly respecting his needful affairs: (IAar, O, L, K: *) and A_ilayohi rasuwlahu ↓ he sent forward, or in advance, his messenger to him, and hastened him: (K, TA: [in the CK, instead of waA^aEojalahu , we find wAarosalahu :]) but [SM says,]

; or he abstained, or desisted, from it: (TA:) and fr~T fiyhi he neglected it; and preferred backwardness ( qad~ama AlEajozi ) in it, or with respect to it; and failed, or fell short, of doing what he ought, or flagged, or was remiss, with respect to it; as also fr~Thu ; (K; [but accord. to the TA, only the former of these two phrases signifies “ he failed of doing what he ought, ” &c.;]) or simply he neglected it; (ISd, TA;) or he failed of doing what he ought, or flagged, or was remiss, with respect to it, and neglected it, (S, O, Msb,) so that it escaped him; (S, O;) as also fyh ↓ , (S, O, K, * [in the K, the words rendered “ so that it escaped him ” are omitted,]) aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. faroTN : (S, O, K:) and fr~T alone, he flagged, or was remiss; was lazy, or indolent: (TA:) its seco

; or granted him a delay, or respite; [and so ↓ ; for] A^aTalotu firaATahumo means I long let them alone, or left them, or granted them delay or respite. (TA.) ― -b5- You say also, fr~T A@ll~`h Eanohu maA yakorahu God put away, or removed, or averted, from him what he dislikes, or hates: (Kh, S, O, K:) but this expression is seldom used except in poetry. (S, O.) -A2- fr~Thu , (O, K,) inf. n. taforiyTN , (TA,) also signifies He praised him immoderately; (O, K, TA;) like qr~Zhu : (O, TA:) Sgh has expressed, in the TS, his fear that the former may be a mistranscription for the latter; but seems to have afterwards conceded the correctness of the former, from his mention of it in the O. (TA.)

3 , (S, O, * K, * in the O and K fArThu ,) inf. n. mufaAraTapN and firaATN , (S,) He vied, or strove, with them, to precede them; to outgo, or outstrip, them; to get before them. (S, O, * K. *) ― -b2- takal~ama firaATFA , (S, O, Msb, K,) the latter word being an inf. n. of fArT , (TA,) He spoke hastily; without premeditation; expl. by sabaqato minohu kalimapN ; (S, O, K;) he let fall hasty, or unpremeditated, sayings or expressions; expl. by saqaTa minohu bawaAdiru . (Msb.) ― -b3- See also 2, in two places: ― -b4- and see
6. ― -b5- fArThu also signifies He found him; syn. A^alofaAhu and SaAdafahu : (O, K, TA:) and so fAlThu and lAfThu . (TA.)

(TA.) And you say also, ↓ waladahu He was preceded by his child to Paradise. (IKtt.) (S, O, K.) [See AiHot

; or made him to hasten. (S, O.) ; or acted extravagantly, or immoderately; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) fiY AlA^amori in the affair; (S, O, TA;) and fY Hub~ihi in loving him; and fY bugoDihi in hating him; (O, TA;) and fY madoHihi in praising him: (K:) it is likewise said of anything exceeding the due bounds; [meaning it was, or became, excessive, or immoderate: ] and also signifies he did more than he was commanded. (S, O. *) Bishr says, [using the verb transitively,] yunaAziEona AlA^aEin~apa muSoEabaAtK kamaA yatafaAraTu Alv~amada AlHamaAmu [ They contend with the reins, being unbroken and refractory, like as the pigeons vie, one with another, in striving to get first to the scanty remains of rainwater ]. (TA.)

Excess; extravagance; exorbitance; an exceeding degree; an exceeding of the due bounds, or just limits. (S, O, K, * TA.) You say, A_iy~aAka waAlfaroTa fiY AlA^amori [ Avoid thou, or beware thou of, excess in the affair ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- Mastery, ascendency, prevalence, or predominance: (K, TA:) as, for instance, of eager desire, and of grief. (TA.) -A2- A time, whether long or short; an indefinite time; syn. HiynN . (S, O, K.) You say, laqiytuhu fiY AlfaroTi baEoda AlfaroTi I met him time after time. (S, O.) And A^anaA A=tiyhi AlfaroTa I come to him, or will come to him, at some time. (TA.) ― -b2- It also denotes one's meeting a man, (TA,) or coming to him, (K,) after some days, (K, TA,) accord. to A 'Obeyd; (TA;) not more than fifteen days, (K,) or than fifteen nights, accord. to the same

A person who goes before, or in advance of, others, to the water, (S, Mgh, K,) or who is sent before, or in advance, to seek water, (Msb,) and who prepares for them the ropes and buckets, (S, O, Msb,) and plasters with mud [in one copy of the S and fills ] the watering-troughs, and draws water for them; (S, TA;) as also ↓ ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA;) being of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure faAEilN , (S, Msb, TA,) like tabaEN in the sense of taAbiEN : (S, TA:) and a number of persons who perform that office; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ , (S, Msb, K, TA,) pl. of faAriTN : (Msb, TA:) you say rajulN faraTN and qawomN faraTN . A swift horse; (S, O, K;) one that precedes, outgoes, outstrips, or gets before, others: (S, A, O:) pl. A^aforaATN . (L, TA.) ― -b2- A case, or an affair, in which the due bounds, or just limits, are exceeded: (S, O, K:) or neglected; (S, * TA;) as also ↓ : (TA:) or despised and neglected. (AHeyth, O, TA.) You say, kul~u A^amori fulaAnK furuTN The whole of the case of such a person is one in which the due bounds, or just limits, are exceeded. (A, TA.) And it is said in the Kur [xviii. 27], wakaAna A^amoruhu furuTFA , meaning, And whose case is one in which the due bounds, or just limits, are exceeded: (S, O:) or in which obedience is neglected and unheeded: (TA:) or [ one of ] preference of backwardness ( taqodiymu AlEajozi ): (Zj:) or [ one of ] repentance: or, accord. to some, the meanin
A single act of going forth; (S, O, K;) and of preceding, or going before. (S, O.) ― -b2- [ A hasty, or an unpremeditated, saying, or action: pl. faraTaAtN . (See

3.)] You say, Aall~`hum~a A@gofiro liY faraTaAtiY , i. e. maA faraTa min~iY [meaning, O God, forgive me my hasty, or unpremeditated, sayings, or actions ]: (TA:) [or my acts of hastiness, or forwardness, and transgression: for] AlfaroTapu fiY Ald~iyni [unless we should in this instance read AlfuroTap , as the Turkish translator of the K has done,] signifies hastiness, or forwardness, and transgression, in religion. The act of going forth; (S, O, K; *) and of preceding, or going before. (S, O.) Hence the saying of Umm-Selemeh, to 'Áïsheh, nahaAki Eani AlfuroTapi fiY AlbilaAdi [ He (referring to Mohammad) forbade thee from going forth into the country, or provinces ]. (S, O.) and furaTiY~N , (Ibn-'Abbád, K,) but the latter is said in the Moheet to be with damm, [which most probably means that it is furoTiY~N , and it is thus written in the O,] (TA,) applied to a camel and to a man, Untractable, refractory, or stubborn; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) not rendered manageable or submissive. (TA.)

(S, O) and ↓ , like vumaAmapN , or ↓ , (so in the O,) Water that is for him, of the tribes, who first arrives at it; (S, O;) water that is common property among a number of tribes, and is for him who first arrives at it: (O, K:) and in like manner the latter word applied to a well. (TA.) You say, bayona baniY fulaAnK ↓ wabaniY fulaAnK , meaning, [ This is water between the sons of such a one and the sons of such a one, so that ] whichever of them arrives at it first waters [ his beasts ] and the others do not throng him. : see firaATN , in three places.

Preceding; going before; being, or becoming, before, beforehand, first, or foremost; having, or getting, priority, or precedence: pl. fur~aATN . (TA.) ― -b2- See the sing. and pl. voce faraTN , first sentence. ― -b3- fur~aATu AlqaTaA The foremost of the [ birds called ] qTA [meaning sand-grouse ], who precede the others to the valley and the water. (S, TA.) ― -b4- faAriTN also signifies One who goes before to dig the grave: pl. as above, and also fawaAriTu , which latter is extr., like fawaArisu , pl. of faArisN , as is said in the O. Sent before, or first, or foremost. (TA.) Hence the saying in the Kur [xvi. 64], (TA,) waA^an~ahumo muforaTuwna And that they shall be sent before, or first, or foremost, to the fire [of Hell], and hastened thither; (Az, O, K, TA;) this being the primary signification: (Az, O, TA:) or forgotten (Mujáhid, Fr, O) in the fire [of Hell]: (Fr:) or neglected, or left: (TA:) or forgotten, and neglected or left, in the fire: and another reading is ↓ , meaning [they are] exceeding the limits assigned to them: (O, K:) and another is ↓ , meaning [ falling short of their duty ] to themselves, in respect of sins. (TA.) ― -b2- [ Filled, or] full; applied to a pool of water left by a torrent. (S, TA.)

Exceeding the due bounds, or just limits; acting extravagantly; applied to a man: excessive; applied to anything; as, for instance, tallness, and shortness. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, ↓ Thou wilt not see the ignorant otherwise than exceeding the due bounds in what he doth or falling short of what he ought therein. (TA.) See also muforaTN .
: see muforaTN and muforiTN .
The extremities of a country or the like. (TA.)
[ Such a one's emulation is foremost in attaining to eminence ]; i. e. he has precedence therein: [see 1, first sentence:] (TA:) said in praise of a man. (TA in art. rnq .)

: see faArigN . ― -b2- *ahaba damuhu firogFA and ↓ mean His blood went for nothing, as a thing of no account, unretaliated, and uncompensated by a mulct, (S, O, K,) and retaliation for it was not sought: (S, O:) and in like manner one says, *ahabato dimaAw^uhumo firgFA [ Their bloods went for nothing, &c.]. (Z, TA.)

Hence, in the Kur xxviii. 9, accord. to one reading, waA^aSobaHa fuw^aAdu A^um~i muwsaY firogFA (Ksh and Bd) i. e. And the heart, or mind, of the mother of Moses became [ as though it were ] a thing that was lost, or that had gone away. (Ksh. [See faArigN .])
: see faArigN , first quarter.

i. q. mufar~agN [ Made empty, vacant, void, &c.]: (O, TA:) so in the phrase A_inaA='N furugN [ An emptied vessel ]: (TA:) and so in the saying [in the Kur xxviii. 9], accord. to the reading of Kh, waA^aSobaHa fuw^aAdu A^um~i muwsaY furugFA [ And the heart of the mother of Moses became rendered void of patience, or of anxiety, &c.: see faArigN ]. (O, TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a bow, as also ↓ , it means Without a string: or, as some say, without an arrow. (TA.)
[whether with or without tenween is not shown] A wide, or capacious, vessel. (TA.)

[generally mentioned as an inf. n., and much used as such; but accord. to the Msb, a simple subst.: as a simple subst., it means Emptiness, vacancy, or vacuity, &c.: ― -b2- and vacancy, or freedom, from business, &c.
; or contr. of $ugolN , as is said in the K, in art. $gl : and cessation from an affair: ― -b3- &c.: see 1]. ― -b4- [ bayotu AlfaraAgi means The privy. ]

A great bowl, that cannot be carried: pl. A^aforigapN . (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b2- A wide, or capacious, large, watering-trough, of hides. (As, O, K.) ― -b3- A vessel (IAar, T, O, K) of any kind. (IAar, T, O.) ― -b4- An udder. (O.) ― -b5- The half of a load, such as is on either of the two sides of a camel: (AA, O, K:) so in the dial. of Teiyi. (AA, O.) ― -b6- See also farogN , second sentence. -A2- [As a pl.,] Valleys, or torrent-beds: from IAar, who has not mentioned a sing. thereof, nor the derivation. (TA.) ― -b2- And [probably as pl. of ↓ , agreeably with analogy,] Broad niSaAl [or arrow-heads; the word nSAl being app. understood]. (O, K.) -A3- [As a sing. epithet,] A she-camel having no brand, or mark made with a hot iron. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A she-camel having much milk, ample in the

Broad, or wide. (TA.) See firaAgN . [Hence,] DarobapN fariygN (S) or fariygapN (O, K) (tropical:) A wide [ wound made by a ] stroke, or blow; (S, O, K, TA;) likened to the farog of the leathern bucket: (TA:) and ↓ , likewise, signifies (tropical:) a wide [ wound made by a ] piercing [with a spear &c.], (S, O, K, TA,) of which the blood flows. (TA.) ― -b2- And fariygapN (tropical:) A mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag] that takes in much water; (O, K, TA;) as though having farog , i. e. width. (TA.) ― -b3- And friygN signifies also (tropical:) Land, or ground, that is even, or flat, as though it were a road, (O, K, TA,) and wide: (TA:) or that is marked by much treading: to such Aboo-Kebeer El-Hudhalee likens the whiteness of the A^avor , i. e. firinod , of a sword. (O, TA.) -A2- And (tropical
The sperma of a man. (S, ISd, K.)

Empty, vacant, void, devoid, destitute, or unoccupied; syn. xaAlK ; as in the phrase A_inaA='N fArigN [ an empty vessel ]: (O, TA:) and likewise applied to a man, (O, TA, *) meaning vacant from, devoid of, or free from, business, occupation, or employment; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ : (O, K, TA:) [and often, used elliptically, meaning vacant from, devoid of, or free from, business &c., and care or anxiety or disquietude; unoccupied, unemployed, or at leisure: ] and ↓ is syn. with faArigN ; (O, K;) as in the phrase, of Ru-beh, maA Alma$oguwlu mivolu AlA^aforagi [ The busied is not like the free from business ]: (O, TA:) [ fur~aAgN is pl. of faArigN : and] ↓ is syn. with fur~aAgN ; (O, K; [in the former, as is often the case, the sign of tesh-deed in this word has been carelessly omitted; and in t

[ More, and most, empty &c.: and more, and most, free from business &c.]. A^aforagu mino fuw^aAdi A^um~i muwsaY [ More void than the heart, or mind, of the mother of Moses ] is a prov. (Meyd. [See faArigN , latter half.]) See also another prov., voce Haj~aAmN . -A2- Also i. q. faArigN , q. v.: (O, K:) fem. farogaA='u : see fariygN .

A place of pouring out or forth: (O, TA:) and [particularly] the part of the leathern bucket that is next to the fore part of the wateringtrough. (TA.) See farogN , second sentence. -A2- Also i. q. sylAn [app. sayalaAnN i. e. The flowing of water &c.; as an inf. n. of fariga said of water]. (TA.)

A dirhem [ cast, i. e.] poured into a mould; not maDoruwb [ coined or minted ]. (TA.) And HaloqapN muforagapN A ring that is solid (S, O, K, TA) in the sides [ that compose the round ], (S, O,) and [ continuous, ] not cut. (TA.) One says, humo kaA@loHaloqapi Almuforagapi laA yudoraY A^ayona TarafaAhaA [ They are like the solid and continuous ring, of which it is not known where are the two ends ]: (A, TA:) a prov., applied to a company of men united in words and action. (TA in art. Hlq .) -A2- muforagN is also an inf. n. of A^aforagahu [q. v.]. (O.)

A she-camel having much milk. (O, K. [See also firaAgN .]) ― -b2- And musotaforigN (tropical:) A horse that does not reserve aught of his run [i. e. of his power of running, for the time of need; that exhausts his power thereof ]. (O, K, TA.)

senses.text: (S, A, L, K) and ↓ , (L,) [the former app. a coll. gen. n., and the latter the n. un., Purslane, or garden purslane; ] the herb called Albaqolapu AlHamoqaA='u , (S, A, L,) which does not grow in Nejd, (L,) also called farofiynN , (S, A,) i. q. rijolapN : (S, L, K:) an arabicized word, from the Pers. ParoPahon , which signifies “ broad-winged. ” (AHn, L, K.) ― -b2-
Also, the former, The kaEaAbir [which are things that are taken forth, or picked out, and thrown away, in the clearing ] of wheat. (K.)
: see the preceding paragraph.

senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, *) aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and in one dial. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. farogN and furoqaAnN , (S, O, Msb, K,) the latter of which has a more intensive signification, (TA,) He made a separation, or a distinction, or difference, (Msb, K, TA,) between the two things, (K, * TA,) or between the parts of the two things: (Msb:) relating alike to objects of sight and to objects of mental perception: (TA:) IAar, by exs. that he mentions, makes it to relate particularly to objects of the mind, such as sayings; and ↓ , to persons, or material things: (Msb: [and it is stated in the Mgh that the same distinction is mentioned by Az:]) others, however, state that the two verbs are syn.; but that the latter has an intensive signification. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [v. 28], faA@foruqo

; or this, he says, may mean the same as the former reading, for sometimes faEala has the same meaning as faE~ala . (TA.) IJ also says that faraqa lahu Eani Al$~aYo'i signifies He made the thing distinct, or plain, to him. (TA.) ― -b2- faraqa Al$~aEora biAlmu$oTi , aor. and , inf. n. faroqN , He separated his hair with the comb: and raA^osahu biAlmu$oTi ↓ , inf. n. taforiyqN , He separated the hair of his head with the comb. (TA.) [And it is implied in a trad. cited in the O and TA that faraqahu signifies the same as the latter of the two phrases in the next preceding sentence.] -A2- faraqa lahu AlT~ariyqu , (S, O, K,) inf. n. furuwqN , (K,) The road presented itself to him divided into two roads: (S, O, K, TA:) or [it means] an affair presented itself, or occurred, to him, and he knew the

; or was, or became, in fear, afraid, or frightened. (S, O, Msb, K.) You say, fariqotu minoka [ I feared thee, or was in fear of thee ]: (S, O, Msb: *) but you should not say, fariqotuka : (S, O:) Sb [however] mentions fariqahu , suppressing mino . (TA.) And you say also, fariqa Ealayohi [ He feared for him ]. (TA.) -A8- And fariqa , aor. , He entered into a wave, [which is termed firoqN ,] and dived therein. (K.) -A9- And the same verb accord. to the K, but accord. to Sgh [in the O] it seems, from the context to be faraqa , (TA,) He drank (O, K) the measure called faraq , (O,) or with the faraq . (K, TA.)
2 , inf. n. taforiyqN and taforiqapN , (S, O, K,) He separated it [ into several, or many, portions ]; disunited it [i. e. a thing, or a collection of things]
; or dispersed, or dissipated, it

; or did so much [or greatly or widely ]; syn. bad~adahu . (K.) And fr~q bayona AlA^a$oyaA='i [ He made, or caused, a separation &c., or much, or a wide, separation, &c., between the things ]. (Mgh.) [And fiyhimo fr~qhu and Ealayohimo He scattered, or distributed, it among them, and to them. ] See 1, former half, in five places. It is said in a trad. of 'Omar, far~iquwA Eani Almaniy~api waA@joEaluwA Alr~aA^osa raA^osayoni , (Mgh, O, *) meaning Separate ye your cattle by way of preservation from death, [ and make the one head two head, ] by buying two animals with the price of one, that, when one dies, the second may remain. (Mgh, O.) And it is said in a trad. respecting the poor-rate, laA yufar~aqu bayona mujotamiEK walaA yujomaEu bayona mufotariqK There shall be no separating what is put
1 in that art.) In the saying in the Kur [ii.

130 and iii. 78], laA nufar~iqu bayona A^aHadK minohumo [ We will not make a distinction between any of them ], the verb is allowably made to relate to AHd because this word [in negative phrases] imports a pl. meaning. (TA. [See p. 27, 3rd col.]) See, again, 1, near the middle. -A2- fr~qhu , (O, TA,) inf. n. taforiyqN , (O, K, TA,) also signifies He made him to fear, or be afraid; put him in fear

; or frightened him: (O, K, * TA:) and minohu ↓ I made him to fear, or be afraid of, him, or it: (Msb:) and Lh mentions AlSabiY~a ↓ as meaning I frightened the boy, or child; but ISd says, I think it to be far~aqotu . (TA.)
3 , inf. n. mufaAriqapN and firaAqN , (S, Msb, TA,) He separated himself from him, or it

; or left, forsook, or abandoned, him, or it: or he forsook, or abandoned, him, being forsaken, or abandoned, by him: syn. baAyanahu ; (TA;) and qaATaEahu , and faArazahu ; (A in art. frz ;) and tarakahu . (Msb in art. trk .) And fArq A@moraA^atahu He separated himself from his wife. (TA.) ― -b2- faAraqotu fulaAnFA mino HisaAbiY EalaY ka*aA waka*aA I released such a one from my reckoning with him on such and such terms agreed upon by both: and so SaAdarotuhu EalaY ka*aA waka*aA . (TA.) And fuwriqa EalaY maAlK yuw^ad~iyhi He (an agent) was released from being reckoned with on the condition of his paying certain property for which he became responsible. (TA in art. Sdr .) -A2- faAraqaniY fafaraqotuhu : see 1, last quarter.

4 They left their camels in the place of pasture, and did not assist them in bringing forth, nor have them got with young. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b2- And Afrq ganamahu He made, or caused, his sheep, or goats, to stray; and neglected them, or caused them to become lost, or to perish. (TA.) ― -b3- And Afrq He lost a portion of his sheep or goats. (IKh, TA.) ― -b4- And His sheep, or goats, became a fariyqap [q. v.]. (IKh, TA.) -A2- Afrq He recovered; (Lth, As, Az, S, O, K;) or recovered, but not completely; (As, O, K;) to which IKh adds, quickly; (TA;) i. e., a sick person from ( mino ) his sickness; (As, Az, S, O, K;) and one fevered from his fever; (As, S;) and one smitten with the plague: (Lth, TA:) or (K) it is not said except in the case of a disease that does not attack one more than once, as

5 , inf. n. tafar~aqN (O, K) and tifir~aAqN , (K, TA,) with two kesrehs, but accord. to the “ Nawádir ” of Lh taforiyqN , (TA,) [and in the CK taforAq ,] It was, or became, separated, or disunited: or separated much, or greatly, or widely, or into several, or many, portions

; or dispersed, or dissipated: contr. of tajam~aEa : and ↓ signifies the same: (K, TA:) and so does ↓ : (TA:) all are quasi-pass. of far~aqotuhu : (S, * TA:) [or rather the second and third have the former of the meanings mentioned above: and tfr~q has the latter of those meanings:] or ↓ is said of two sayings, as quasi-pass. of faraqotu bayonahumaA : and tafar~aqaA , of two men, as quasi-pass. of far~aqotu bayonahamaA : (Mgh, * Msb, TA:) so says IAar: (Msb:) [but] one says also, Aftrq Alqawomu [ The party, or company of men, became separated

; or they separated themselves: ] (Msb:) and Esh-Sháfi'ee has used ↓ as relating to two persons buying and selling; (Msb, TA;) and so have Ahmad [Ibn-Hambal] and Aboo-Haneefeh and Málik and others. (TA.) It is said in a trad., Albay~aEaAni biAlxiyaAri maA yatafar~aqaA i. e. [ The buyer and seller have the option to annul their contract] as long as they have not become separated bodily; (Mgh, Msb;) originally, maA lamo yatafar~aqo A^abodaAnuhumaA ; for this is the proper meaning. (Msb.) tafar~aqato bihimu AlT~uruqu [properly The roads became separate with them, ] means every one of them went one [ separate ] way. (TA.) [And one says, tfr~qt AlA^agoSaAnu (S in art. $*b , &c.,) The branches were, or became, or grew out, apart, one from another; divaricated; diverged; forked; straggled

; or spread widely and dispersedly. And tfr~q A^amoruhu His affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, disorganized, disordered, or unsettled, so that he considered what might be its issues, or results, saying at one time, I will do thus, and at another time, I will do thus: see A^ajomaEa ; and $at~a : and ↓ signifies the same: see an ex. voce fa$aA , in art. f$w . And tfr~qt kalimatuhumo (K voce $aAla , in art. $wl ,) Their expression of opinion was, or became, discordant: and tfr~qt A=raAw^uhumo Their opinions were, or became, so. ]
6 They separated themselves, one from another
; or left, forsook, or abandoned, one another. (TA.)
7 , of which munofaraqN may be an inf. n. [like AinofiraAqN ], as well as a n. of place, It was, or became, separated, or divided. (O, K.) See also
5. [Hence,] Anfrq Alfajoru i. q. Ainofalaqa [ The dawn broke ]. (TA.)
8 : see 5, first sentence, in three places: and also in the last sentence but one.

[is originally an inf. n.: but is often used as a simple subst. meaning A distinction, or difference, between two things. ― -b2- Hence,] The line [or division ] in the hair of the head: (K: [see also maforaqN :]) or, as some say, the part, of the head, extending from the side of the forehead to the spiral curl upon the crown: an ex. occurs in a verse of Aboo-Dhu-eyb cited voce maTorabN . (TA.) ― -b3- [And app. A blaze on a horse's forehead. (See an ex. voce muEotadilN .)] ― -b4- And [hence, perhaps,] one says, baAnato fiY qa*aAlihi furuwqN mina Al$~ayobi i. e. A^awoDaAHN [app. meaning There appeared in the back of his head portions of white, or hoary, hair, distinct from the rest ]. (TA.) ― -b5- One says also of the female comber and dresser of the hair, tamo$uiTu ka*aA waka*aA faroqFA i.

: see AlfuroqaAnu . ― -b2- It also signifies A certain vessel with which one measures. (TA. [See also faraqN .]) ― -b3- And [it is said that] AlfuroqaAni signifies qdHAn mftrqAn [app. meaning Two separate bowls, or milking-vessels, supposing the former word to be qadaHaAni ; the latter word being mufotariqaAni ]. (TA. [This is app. said in explanation of furoqaAni ending a verse in which it means “ milkingvessels: ” but it is said in the S, and in one place in the TA, that it is in that instance pl. of faroqN or faraqN , q. v.])

A piece, or portion, that is split from a thing, or cleft therefrom; (S, O, K;) whence its usage in the Kur xxvi. 63: (S, O:) and a portion of anything (K, TA) when it is separated; and the pl. is firaqN : (TA:) or a portion that is separated, or dispersed, of a thing; and thus it is said to mean in the Kur ubi suprá; and the pl. is A^aforaAqN , like A^aHomaAlN as pl. of HimolN . (Msb.) See also firoqapN . ― -b2- Also A great flock or herd, of sheep or goats: (S, O, K:) and (as some say, TA) of the bovine kind: or of gazelles: or of sheep, or goats, only: or of straying sheep or goats; as also ↓ , (K, TA,) and ↓ : (TA:) or less than a hundred, (K, TA,) of sheep or goats. (TA.) firoqaAni mino TayorK SawaAf~a , occurring in a trad., in which the second and third chapters of the Kur-án are li

4.] -A2- Also A mountain. (IAar, O, K.) And A [ hill, or mountain, or the like, such as is termed ] haDobap . (IAar, O, K.) ― -b2- And A wave, billow, or surge. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b3- And Alfiroqu is the name applied by the Arabs to The star [a] upon the right shoulder of Cepheus. (Kzw.)

Wideness of the space between the two central incisors, (IKh, S, O, K, TA,) of a man: (TA:) and likewise between the two toe-nails of the camel. (Yaakoob, S, O, K, TA.) And A division in the Eurof [or comb ] of the cock: and likewise in the forelock, and in the beard, of a man: (S, O, K:) pl. A^aforaAqN . (S, O.) And sparseness, or a scattered state, of the plants, or herbage, of a land. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- In a horse, The state of the hips when one of them is more prominent than the other; which is disapproved: (S, O, K, TA:) or a deficiency in one of the thighs, in comparison with the other: or a deficiency in one of the hips. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The dawn: or Alfaraqu signifies falaqu AlS~uboHi : (K:) or what has broken of the bright gleam of dawn; of the dawn that rises and spreads, filling

Also, and ↓ , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) the latte accord. to the usage of the relaters of traditions, (Az, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) but the former accord. to the usage of the Arabs, (Az, Mgh, O, * TA,) or the former is the more chaste (K, TA) accord. to Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà and Khálid Ibn-Yezeed, (TA,) A certain vessel, (T, Mgh, O, Msb,) a measure of capacity, (S, O, K, TA,) of large size, (TA,) well known, (S,) in El-Medeeneh, (S, Msb, K,) holding three A=SuE [a pl. of SaAEN ], (Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) or, (K, [app. referring to ↓ only,]) which is the same quantity, sixteen pints, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, * TA,) i. e. twelve times the quantity termed mud~ by the people of El-Hijáz: (TA:) or, accord. to El-Kutabee, the ↓ is sixteen pints, and the SAE is one third of the faroq ; but the faraq is eighty pints: or th
: see faruwqapN , in two places.
is applied to plants, or herbage, ( nabotN ,) as meaning [ In a sparse, or scattered, state

; or] small, not covering the ground: (AHn, K, TA:) or (K) fariqapN is applied to land, ( A^aroDN ,) meaning of which the plants, or herbage, are in a sparse, or scattered, state; (S, O, K, TA;) not contiguous: (S, O, TA:) thus used, it is a possessive epithet, having no verb. (TA.) -A2- See also faruwqapN , in two places.

the subst. from faAraqahu ; (S, MA, * TA;) or from Aifotaraqa , (Msb,) [i. e.] a quasi-inf. n. used in the sense of AifotiraAqN ; (TA;) signifying Separation, disunion, or abandonment; (MA, KL, PS;) and ↓ is syn. therewith, whence the reading [in the Kur xviii. 77], h`*aA faraAqu bayoniY wabayonika [ This shall be the separation of my and thy union ]; and so is ↓ , (O, * K, TA,) which [is an inf. n. of fArqh , and], in the Kur lxxv. 28, means the time of the quitting of the present world by death. (TA.)

A TaAy^ifap [or party, portion, division, sect, or distinct body or class, ] of men, (S, O, Msb, K,) and of other things; as also ↓ ; (Msb;) and so, accord. to IB, ↓ : (TA: [but see this last word:]) [and a separate herd or the like of cattle:] pl. firaqN (O, Msb, K) and A^aforaAqN (S, O, K) is pl. of firaqN (O, K) and A^afaAriyqu is pl. of A^aforaAqN , (S, O, K,) and A^afaAriqapN occurs in poetry; (O, K;) or A^afaAriyqu may be of the class of A^abaATiylu , a pl. without a sing. (O, TA.) ― -b2- Also A portion of a thing in a state of dispersion; and so ↓ and ↓ . (L, TA.) -A2- And A skin that is full [ of milk ], that cannot be agitated to make butter Hat~aY A^aYo yu*oraqa ↓ [app. a tropical phrase meaning until it is made to void some of its contents ]. (K.)
, originally an inf. n. (Msb. [See 1, first sentence.]) Anything that makes a separation, or distinction, between truth and falsity. (S, O, K.) ― -b2-

Hence, (TA,) AlfuroqaAnu signifies The Kur-án; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ . (S, O, K.) ― -b3- And The Book of the Law revealed to Moses, (Az, O, K,) in which a distinction is made between that which is allowable and that which is forbidden. (O.) ― -b4- And Proof, evidence, or demonstration. (O, K.) ― -b5- And The time a little before daybreak: (AA, O, K:) or the dawn. (O, K.) One says, TalaEa AlfuroqaAnu [ The dawn rose ]. (O.) ― -b6- And Aid, or victory: (IDrd, O, K:) so, accord. to IDrd, in the phrase yawoma AlfuroqaAni in the Kur [viii. 42]: (O:) or by this phrase is meant The day of Bedr, (O, K,) in which a distinction was made between right and wrong. (O.) ― -b7- And The cleaving of the sea: so it means [accord. to some] in the Kur ii.
50. (O, K.) ― -b8- And Boys: (O, K:) such the people of the olden time used to make witnesses [in law-suits or the like]. (O.) -A2- It is also pl. of faroqN (S, M, O, K) and of faraqN . (S, Mgh, O.)
and firaAqN : see furoqapN .
: see faruwqapN , in two places: -A2- and A^aforaqu , last sentence but two.

A TaAy^ifap [or party, &c.,] (S, Msb, K) more in number, (S, K, *) or larger, (Msb,) than a firoqap : (S, Msb, K:) pl.
